issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping under load, flaring revs between gears, late or harsh shifts, no fourth gear, or the car eventually refusing to move. The fluid may look dark or smell burnt.
issues.why: These cars pair a strong 4.6L V8 with a front-drive automatic originally designed for smaller V6 engines. Clutches and the torque converter wear out early, especially when the fluid is rarely changed or the car is driven hard. Failures most often show up between about 55,000 and 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it is slipping, stop hard driving and get a transmission shop diagnosis; a rebuilt or used unit is usually the fix. Regular fluid changes and an add-on cooler help a replacement last longer.

issues.t: Air suspension sags or compressor fails
issues.sym: The car sits low, usually at the rear, after parking or even while driving. You may see a "Check Air Suspension" message, hear the compressor running a long time, or notice a harsh ride and headlights aimed too high.
issues.why: The rubber air springs crack and leak with age, and the compressor then wears out trying to keep up. Height sensors and air lines can also fail. 1995-1996 models use air at all four corners; 1997-2002 use air at the rear only.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks before replacing the compressor, or the new one will fail too. Replacing the leaking air springs fixes it; many owners convert to conventional springs to avoid repeat repairs.

issues.t: Front coil spring breaks and cuts the tire
issues.sym: A loud pop or bang, often when backing up or turning, followed by a flat front tire. The car may lean at one front corner.
issues.why: The front coil springs on this generation can snap, and the broken end can slice into the inner sidewall of the tire. Several owners reported it happening at low speed, at anywhere from about 50,000 to 160,000 miles.
issues.next: If you hear a bang from the front and the car sits unevenly, don't drive it. Replace springs in pairs and inspect the tire, strut and sway bar link for damage.

issues.t: Shudder or torque converter not locking up
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration at light throttle, often around 35-55 mph or during the 3-4 shift, and sometimes a check engine light. Fuel economy may drop.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch either slips or fails to engage. Ford issued service bulletins for the shudder and for the converter not engaging on this transmission.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. A fluid exchange and software update sometimes help; a worn converter has to be replaced.

issues.t: Clunk or harsh engagement shifting out of Park
issues.sym: A clunk or bump when you shift out of Park, especially on a hill, or a harsh jolt when shifting from Park or Neutral into Drive.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for park pullout clunk on this transmission. A failing neutral-drive accumulator inside the transmission can also make engagements harsh.
issues.next: Mention it at your next service. If engagements are getting harsher, have the transmission checked before it leads to bigger damage.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leaking from seals
issues.sym: Red fluid spots under the front of the car, low transmission fluid, and slipping if the level gets too low.
issues.why: Seals on the transmission and torque converter hub can leak on these cars. Owners report leaks around 69,000 miles, sometimes on a replacement transmission.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and top it up. Have the leak located; driving low on fluid can destroy the transmission.

issues.t: Car can roll while in Park (1996 recall)
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park, but the car can roll as if in Neutral.
issues.why: The parking pawl shaft may not move freely, so the pawl does not lock the transmission.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake. Have a Lincoln dealer check that recall 96V176 was done; the shaft is replaced free.

issues.t: Car can roll while in Park (1997 recall)
issues.sym: The gear indicator shows Park, but the car can still move.
issues.why: A sharp edge on the park pawl bracket can stop the pawl from engaging.
issues.next: Use the parking brake, and have a dealer confirm recall 96V166 was completed; the bracket is replaced free.

issues.t: Headlights can shut off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: With the automatic headlight setting on, the headlights go out without warning.
issues.why: A faulty autolamp control module can switch the headlamps off.
issues.next: Use the manual headlight switch until a dealer confirms recall 96V009 was done (the module is replaced free).

issues.t: Headlights only work on high beam
issues.sym: The low beams quit while the high beams still work.
issues.why: Owners trace this to the headlamp control module or its wiring. Average mileage in reports is about 83,000.
issues.next: Check the bulbs and fuses first. If those are fine, have the headlamp control module tested.

issues.t: Door ajar warning and dome light stay on
issues.sym: The door ajar light, warning chime or interior lights stay on with all doors closed, which can drain the battery overnight.
issues.why: A door latch switch wears or sticks so the car thinks a door is open. This is the most-reported complaint on the 1999 model.
issues.next: Open and firmly close each door to find the one causing it. Replacing that door's latch or ajar switch fixes it.

issues.t: Power steering failure
issues.sym: Steering gets heavy, groans, or loses assist, often with fluid leaks.
issues.why: The power steering pump, hoses or rack can leak and wear. Reported failures average about 106,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and look for leaks. Have the pump and rack inspected; don't keep driving with the reservoir low.

issues.t: Security light flashes and car won't start
issues.sym: The theft light on the dash flashes and the engine will not start, or starts and dies.
issues.why: The anti-theft system is not reading the chip in the key, often from a worn key, failed transceiver ring around the ignition, or a wiring fault.
issues.next: Try a spare key. If the spare works, the original key needs replacing. If neither works, have the anti-theft system checked by a dealer or locksmith.

issues.t: Fuel rail hose can leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell under the hood, or visible fuel wetness on top of the engine.
issues.why: The fuel rail crossover hose was damaged during assembly and can leak, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Do not drive if you smell fuel. Ask a dealer about recall 98V269; the fuel rail is replaced free.

issues.t: Front airbags can deploy from underbody hits (recall)
issues.sym: Front airbags go off after the underside of the car strikes debris or a road hazard.
issues.why: The crash sensors could read underbody impacts, such as debris thrown from the wheels, as a crash.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm recall 03V144 was done; the sensors are recalibrated free.

issues.t: Front seat belt may not pull out or lock for a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: A front seat belt won't pull out, or won't switch into the locking mode used to hold a child seat.
issues.why: A pin in the belt retractor may be misformed.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 99V250; affected belts are replaced free.

issues.t: Wiper motor can overheat or stop (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers stop working, or there is a burning smell from the cowl area.
issues.why: A switch inside the wiper motor gear case can overheat, which can stop the wipers or even ignite the cover.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about recall 01V258; the gear case cover is replaced free.

issues.t: Cruise control goes over the set speed downhill
issues.sym: With cruise control on, the car speeds up past the set speed on downhill grades. Some owners also report a sticking throttle.
issues.why: This is the most-reported 2002 complaint. Owners blame the speed control and throttle, and no recall covers it.
issues.next: Avoid cruise control on long downgrades until it is checked. Have the throttle body cleaned and the speed control system inspected.

issues.t: Misfire and rough running from ignition coils
issues.sym: Check engine light (often flashing), a shaking idle, and hesitation under load.
issues.why: Each cylinder has its own coil on top of the spark plug, and these coils fail with age and heat. Ford issued several diagnostic bulletins for coil-on-plug misfires.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to find the cylinder. A flashing check engine light means stop driving soon, as it can damage the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Oil leak from the oil pan seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the engine, oil residue on the pan, or a burning-oil smell.
issues.why: The sealant (RTV) between the oil pan and engine block can leak on the 2.7L and 3.0L EcoBoost engines. Ford issued several bulletins with a revised resealing procedure.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and ask a Lincoln dealer about the bulletin; it may be covered under the powertrain warranty.

issues.t: White or blue smoke and rough idle on early builds
issues.sym: Puffs of white or blue exhaust smoke, especially after start-up, with a rough idle.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for 2.7L and 3.0L EcoBoost engines built in 2016-2017 that can burn oil this way. Oil reaching the cylinders burns and makes the smoke.
issues.next: Have a Lincoln dealer check it against the bulletin while the car is under warranty. Keep an eye on the oil level.

issues.t: Turbocharger oil line leaks
issues.sym: Oil seeping near the turbochargers, a burning-oil smell, or oil spots under the car.
issues.why: The oil feed and return tubes, O-rings and gaskets for the turbos can leak. Ford issued a bulletin for these leaks.
issues.next: Have the leak located. Oil dripping on hot exhaust parts can smoke or catch fire, so don't ignore it.

issues.t: Vibration from a leaking engine mount
issues.sym: More vibration at idle or under load than before, sometimes with warning lights or codes.
issues.why: The fluid-filled engine mounts can leak and stop damping vibration. Ford issued a bulletin covering mount leaks on the 2.7L and 3.0L.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected for fluid leaks and replace any leaking mount.

issues.t: Check engine light for cam timing codes
issues.sym: Check engine light with cam timing codes (P0011 through P0025), sometimes a rough idle.
issues.why: Debris can make the variable cam timing solenoids stick. Ford issued several bulletins on these codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Keep up oil changes with the right oil; a dealer may replace the solenoids.

issues.t: Doors may not latch and can open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: A door won't close or latch fully, a door ajar warning stays on, or a door opens while the car is moving.
issues.why: The motors in the electronic door latches can fail, so the latch does not fully catch. Lincoln replaces the latches on all four doors under recall 19V077 (19S03).
issues.next: Check for open recalls with your VIN and have it done right away. Make sure each door is fully shut before driving.

issues.t: Door won't open from the handle or button
issues.sym: Pressing the door button or pulling the handle does nothing, from inside or outside. Soft-close doors may not release.
issues.why: These cars use electronic door latches. Ford issued bulletins for door handles that fail to open the door and for soft-close doors that won't open, both tied to latch module faults.
issues.next: Check the recall above first. If it is done, ask a dealer about the door latch bulletins. Learn where the manual release is in case the battery dies.

issues.t: Backup camera image cloudy (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera picture looks foggy or hazy.
issues.why: The coating on the camera lens can break down. Lincoln replaces the camera under recall 22V644.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the camera replaced free.

issues.t: Backup camera goes blank or stays on (recall)
issues.sym: No picture when you shift into Reverse, or the camera view stays on after you shift out.
issues.why: A software fault in the camera system. Lincoln updates the software under recall 25V442.
issues.next: Have the free software update done by a dealer.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not inflate properly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash; the problem shows up only when the airbag deploys.
issues.why: The driver frontal airbag may not fully inflate or its cushion may detach in a crash. Lincoln replaces the module under recall 17V123.
issues.next: Check for open recalls with your VIN and get it done promptly.

issues.t: Paint bubbling on aluminum body panels
issues.sym: Bubbles, blisters or peeling paint, often along the edges of the hood or doors.
issues.why: Corrosion forms under the paint on the aluminum panels. Ford issued bulletins saying affected panels should be replaced, not just repainted.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect it while it is small; paint and corrosion warranties may help.

issues.t: Water on the passenger floor
issues.sym: Wet carpet or standing water in the front passenger footwell, often after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water can get in through the climate system's fresh air inlet. Ford issued a bulletin with a repair.
issues.next: Dry the carpet quickly to prevent mold and electrical problems, and ask a dealer about the bulletin.

issues.t: Weak air conditioning from the A/C compressor
issues.sym: A/C blows warm or not cold enough, or climate control acts oddly. A code P06A0 may be stored.
issues.why: Ford issued several bulletins for the electronically controlled A/C compressor causing poor A/C performance.
issues.next: Have the A/C system checked and ask the dealer about the compressor bulletins.

issues.t: Dead 12-volt battery
issues.sym: The car won't start or cranks slowly after sitting, or warning messages about the battery appear.
issues.why: Ford bulletins cover battery drain from third-party phone apps that keep waking the car, discharged batteries from the CD player, and loose battery terminals.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested. Ask a dealer about software updates and the terminal bulletin.

issues.t: SYNC 3 screen blank, frozen or slow
issues.sym: The center touch screen goes blank or blue, freezes, doesn't respond to touch, or navigation and phone apps act up.
issues.why: Software faults in the SYNC 3 system. Ford issued many bulletins and software updates.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the latest SYNC software update.

issues.t: Driver seat belt locks up
issues.sym: The driver seat belt is hard to pull out or locks up when you lean forward.
issues.why: The belt retractor can bind. Ford issued bulletins for driver belts that lock up and webbing that doesn't pull out properly.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the retractor; a seat belt that won't extend should be fixed right away.
